conditions: Accepted r128 6-step schedule, 512px, fixed seed, locked prompt, identical harness used for every candidate
observable: DINO image cosine and pixel MAE of the regenerated 6-step output against the stored locked 6-step reference
expected_if_focal: Harness reproduces the locked reference within the previously recorded run-to-run nondeterminism (pixel MAE of order 0.015 as already observed)
expected_if_rivals: H-ARTIFACT predicts the harness itself perturbs the sampler path, so a mismatch here would implicate the harness rather than the candidate
falsifier: Reproduced reference differs from the stored reference by far more than the recorded nondeterminism, e.g. pixel MAE above 0.1
indeterminate_result: Result falls in the band between accepted nondeterminism and a gross mismatch; the next step is to re-measure the reference twice before interpreting any candidate
boundary_conditions: Applies only to 512px, the locked prompt set, and the r128 six-step schedule under the accepted INT8 server configuration
uncertainty: Run-to-run nondeterminism of this stack was already observed at pixel MAE 0.0151 without any code change; the discriminating band for a real change is therefore much wider than that

conditions: Identical seed, prompt, conditioning and schedule; generation run twice, once with the trained LoRA injection active and once with the injection removed
observable: Pixel MAE and DINO cosine between the two generated images
expected_if_focal: A correctly wired adapter measurably changes the output, so a quality result attributable to it is interpretable
expected_if_rivals: H-NOOP predicts the two images are identical, which would void every quality claim made from adapter-on runs and would reframe the previous run as untested rather than negative
falsifier: Trained-adapter output is pixel-identical to no-adapter output
indeterminate_result: Difference is below the recorded nondeterminism floor (pixel MAE under 0.0151), in which case the injection is treated as inert and the run is void rather than negative
boundary_conditions: Applies to the BypassInjectionManager path used by the training script; it does not by itself validate any other LoRA path
uncertainty: The previous run reported a trained student slightly worse than untrained, which is equally consistent with an inert injection and with a real but unhelpful gradient; this test separates the two

conditions: Untrained accepted r128 student, one sigma at a time removed from the six-step grid, fixed seed and locked prompt set, no adapter
observable: DINO image cosine versus the locked six-step reference at 6,5,4,3,2 and 1 steps
expected_if_focal: The decline is gradual from 6 to 4 steps and then drops sharply between 3 and 2 steps, locating the cliff
expected_if_rivals: H4-SCHEDULE predicts the decline is an artifact of which nodes were kept, in which case a re-chosen grid at 2 steps also rises sharply
falsifier: The measured curve is flat through 2 steps (DINO at or above 0.9), which contradicts the recorded 0.518 two-step result and points instead at a sampler-path or harness difference
indeterminate_result: If any step in the sweep fails to produce a decodable image, that step is reported as missing and the curve is drawn as a lower bound rather than interpolated
boundary_conditions: Single prompt and single seed characterise one trajectory, not the distribution; the curve is a locus for choosing where to train, not a quality claim
uncertainty: A one-prompt one-seed sweep cannot separate a genuine step-count effect from prompt-specific behaviour; it is used only to locate the cliff, and any training decision must be confirmed on a wider prompt set

conditions: Untrained accepted r128 student, 2-step Euler, grid searched over the first and second shifted sigma, fixed seed and locked prompt
observable: Best attainable DINO cosine over the searched grid, and the identity of the best pair
expected_if_focal: The best searched 2-step grid is close to the recorded 0.518, so the 2-step collapse is not mainly a poor choice of nodes
expected_if_rivals: H1-CLIFF predicts a re-chosen grid is clearly better, meaning a material part of the recorded gap was schedule choice rather than student error
falsifier: Search finds no pair above 0.55 while four-step remains near 0.95
indeterminate_result: The best pair is found only at the edge of the searched range, in which case the search is widened before the result is interpreted
boundary_conditions: Applies to the untrained network only; a trained student's optimal grid may differ and is not determined here
uncertainty: The searched range is a subset of a continuous grid, so this bounds schedule suboptimality within that range only

conditions: Accepted INT8 server, 512px, warm path, prompt varied every request, 2 warmups and at least 5 measured requests per configuration
observable: Text-encode, denoise and VAE seconds plus warm end-to-end median, collected at several step counts
expected_if_focal: Measured non-denoise fixed cost is at least 0.80 s, so the fitted latency at one step stays at or above 1.0 s and step count alone cannot reach the 1 s target
expected_if_rivals: H-NFE-ONLY predicts the fitted one-step latency lands below 1.0 s, which would restore step distillation as a sufficient route
falsifier: A repeated measurement of the fixed cost returns a value low enough that the one-step fitted latency falls below 1.0 s
indeterminate_result: Stage attribution is ambiguous when the sampler fault lands in the denoise stage, in which case the first-step cost is measured separately and reported as its own term
boundary_conditions: Assumes the accepted server configuration; a different cache or offload policy changes the fixed term and invalidates the fit
uncertainty: Per-stage attribution depends on node-level timing reported by the server, which is an engineering measurement rather than a model property; the fitted per-step coefficient is the model-facing quantity

conditions: Objective held fixed to the previously used detached-state MSE, optimizer and update count held fixed, correction rank raised from 1 to 16 and target modules extended from to_out.0 to attention projections plus modulation and timestep embedder
observable: Holdout latent error on seeds never used by the optimizer
expected_if_focal: Holdout error falls materially relative to the rank-1 run, so capacity was a binding constraint
expected_if_rivals: H3-OBJECTIVE predicts holdout error stays flat across ranks, meaning the objective supplies no gradient that extra capacity can use
falsifier: Holdout error is flat from rank 1 to rank 16 under this objective
indeterminate_result: Holdout error falls but the end-to-end quality gate does not move, which would mean the holdout proxy is not tracking image quality and the proxy itself is suspect
boundary_conditions: Separates capacity only under this objective; a capacity result under one objective does not transfer to another
uncertainty: Holdout error is a latent-space proxy and is not assumed to track image quality; the two are compared rather than assumed equivalent

conditions: Capacity held fixed to the same rank and target modules, optimizer and update count held fixed, objective changed from detached midpoint-state and final-latent regression to backpropagation through the student's own two-step rollout
observable: Holdout error on the final denoised latent at seeds never used by the optimizer
expected_if_focal: On-policy rollout backpropagation lowers final-latent holdout error substantially more than the detached objective at equal compute
expected_if_rivals: H2-CAPACITY predicts both objectives plateau at similar holdout error, meaning the gap lies in capacity rather than in the objective
falsifier: The two objectives reach indistinguishable holdout error
indeterminate_result: Rollout backpropagation is not memory-feasible at 512px on this card, in which case the experiment is reported as infeasible rather than as a null result
boundary_conditions: A two-step rollout is assumed; a one-step rollout has no compounding term to correct and is a different experiment
uncertainty: Both objectives are stochastic; the comparison needs enough holdout seeds that the difference is larger than the seed-to-seed spread, which is measured first

conditions: Same procedure and capacity applied as an incremental 6 to 3 step halving, then a 3 to 2 step halving, instead of a single 6 to 2 jump
observable: End-to-end DINO cosine against the locked six-step reference, and holdout latent error
expected_if_focal: Incremental halving reaches a clearly higher two-step quality than the previous single-jump rank-1 result
expected_if_rivals: H2-CAPACITY predicts incremental halving stays near the previous 0.518 because capacity, not reduction factor, was the limit
falsifier: Incremental halving does not exceed the single-jump result by more than run-to-run variation
indeterminate_result: The intermediate three-step student is not reproducible, in which case the ladder claim is unsupported and the single jump is reported as the only result
boundary_conditions: Requires a three-step student to be a valid target, which the cliff location in P1 determines
uncertainty: Two successive halvings cost roughly twice the training compute of one, so a null result here is weaker evidence than a positive one
